analyst_view.overall: Las Palmas (9th, 23 pts) are on the rise since Albert Sánchez took over in early November: four league wins in five, the latest a 0-2 at Sporting on Sunday with goals from Loiodice and Miyashiro. Andorra are 21st with one win in their last five, lost 1-3 at home to Leganés on Friday and now miss two players: goalkeeper Jesús Owono (12-match ban, already counted by the numbers) and midfielder Hugo Solozábal, sent off after 16 minutes against Leganés and banned for this game, which the numbers do not know. Las Palmas still have a long injury list (Enrique Clemente, Sandro with a calf tear, Rafa Cruz, Edward Cedeño), though one injury report expects Sergio Ruiz and Viti to be available again this week. The club calls this 13:00 Saturday game important to win back a home crowd that has fallen below half the stadium. No referee is named yet, so the view rests on form, the bans and the injury news; I lean slightly towards Las Palmas producing more.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already take a little off for Enrique Clemente and add for Andorra's recent leaky defence. I lean slightly higher, 2.8 to about 2.9: Andorra lose Solozábal, a starting midfielder sent off against Leganés, which the numbers don't know, and Las Palmas are scoring freely since the coaching change. Sandro's new calf tear keeps it small.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners, with Las Palmas' recent corner count trimmed by momentum and Andorra's slightly raised. Las Palmas scored from a corner at Sporting and should have more of the ball at home, but nothing in the news changes how either side wins corners. I stay at 8.6.

cards.text: The numbers expect 5.8 cards and already add a lot for Andorra's recent run (25 cards in six games, momentum +18%), which includes two straight reds in recent weeks (Owono and Solozábal). No referee is named yet and I found nothing new beyond what that form already shows, so I stay at 5.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.0 shots, with Las Palmas' own shots trimmed for momentum and Andorra's raised. I lean slightly higher, to about 23.7: without Solozábal Andorra's midfield is thinner, and a home side in form against a team in the bottom two should get more attempts than its recent count suggests. A mild lean only.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target and already credit Andorra's recent accuracy (+8% momentum). For the same reasons as the shots, a weakened Andorra midfield and a Las Palmas side in form, I nudge it up to about 9.3. Andorra's backup goalkeeper situation after Owono's ban is already in the numbers.
